data.description:
## Story

As a developer, I can configure `review.max_cycles` in `.claude/dso-config.conf` to bound the review-resolution loop at a specific cycle count, so that the new arbiter uses consistent, discoverable config terminology.

## Done Definitions

- [ ] `max_resolution_attempts` key is renamed to `max_cycles` in all code paths that read or write it — no remaining references to the old key in production code
- [ ] `read-config.sh` returns the correct value for `review.max_cycles`; old key `review.max_resolution_attempts` is either aliased (with deprecation log) or removed
- [ ] All callers audited: a grep for `max_resolution_attempts` in `.claude/`, `plugins/dso/`, `dso_ci_review/` returns zero hits in code files (skills, scripts, hooks, Python); comments and docs updated separately
- [ ] `.claude/dso-config.conf` sample/default value updated to `review.max_cycles`
- [ ] `CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md` updated: old key name removed, new key documented with same semantics
- [ ] Existing callers that read `review.max_resolution_attempts` at runtime (sprint SKILL.md Step 1, debug-everything, fix-bug, review workflow) verified to use the new key
- [ ] At least one test (unit or integration) confirms that `read-config.sh review.max_cycles` returns the configured value

## Considerations

- [Scope] Audit scope: `grep -r "max_resolution_attempts" plugins/dso/ .claude/` before writing any code — the summary count in the context may be stale; count from source
- [Backward-compat] If any CI pipeline or external consumer reads `max_resolution_attempts`, add a one-cycle alias with a deprecation warning rather than a hard break
- [Atomicity] Key rename touches many files; do all reads/writes in one commit so no intermediate state references both old and new key
- [Escalation policy] Escalate when blocked
data.title: As a developer, I can configure review.max_cycles to bound the review loop at a specific cycle count
